title: Do "Shitty" Work: prioritize what's needed over what's fun
summary: Ryan argues founders gravitate toward their own craft (coding, wireframing) because it feels like progress, while neglecting unglamorous but critical work like talking to customers and acquiring users. He shares his PlayHaven wireframing mistake and a simple fix: ask "why" about every to-do item.

principles.text: Startups need attention in every area, not just your craft; someone must figure out user acquisition.
principles.quote: successful startups require attention in all areas. You may not have a marketing title but someone has to figure out how to acquire users.

principles.text: Founders default to work they like instead of work they should do, because their craft feels comforting.
principles.quote: If we’re not careful, we prioritize things we _like_ to do over the things we _should_ do.

principles.text: Validate market need and talk to customers and engineers before polishing designs for features.
principles.quote: we should have validated the market need and business feasibility rather than waste time pixel shifting for a product no one wanted.

principles.text: Sketch and use paper prototypes first to bring ideas to life in less time.
principles.quote: I should have [sketched](http://ryanhoover.me/post/48834597557/stop-using-wireframe-tools) first and used paper prototypes to bring my ideas to life in less time.

principles.text: Building output (code, wireframes) gives fake progress; marketing and sales have delayed, unpredictable rewards so people avoid them.
principles.quote: People, on the other hand, are often unpredictable and non-responsive.

principles.text: Hold yourself accountable by asking why about every item on your daily to-do list.
principles.quote: The best way to avoid the fake progress trap is to hold yourself accountable. Each morning as you review your morning to-do list, [ask yourself why]
